text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- All papers deal with the celebrations marking the 149th anniversary of the 1848-1849 revolution at the weekend.

- Austrian Chancellor Victor Klima made a brief visit to Budapest on Friday to confer with Prime Minister Gyula Horn on setting up a separate lane for Hungarian citizens at other Austrian border stations than just Hegyeshalom.
- Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus pays a one-day visit to Budapest today.
- Seven women and six children, the families of staff working at the Hungarian embassy in Tirana, were flown home by the German Air Force Friday night.
- The national airlines Malev last year increased the number of its passengers by 21 percent, the highest rate in Europe, said managing director Sandor Szathmary said.
- Hungarian-born painter Victor Vasarely died at a Paris clinic at the weekend, a few days before his 89th birthday.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Farmers' demonstrations will be cut back to one demonstration per county, as spring work on the land begins and farmers await the progress of a bill governing the strategic questions of the agriculture sector.
- The Northern Ireland firm Short Brothers has called for quashing the result of a recent missile tender on technical grounds, and the launch of a new tender.
- A young man in Gyongyos has been taken into custody after he attempted to extort HUF 5 million from the Free Democrats.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- This paper prints an essay by British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind expressing Britain's support for the expansion of the European Union.
- The European integration process has stagnated, said Hungarian-born millionaire George Soros, due to a lack of political support for further steps in the EU.
- Parliament is expected to amend tax and social insurance regulations affecting farmers this week.
- The national oil and gas firm MOL Rt plans to obtain 10 percent of the Austrian petrol market, this paper quotes Austrian press information.
- The Budapest Prosecutor's Office last Thursday questioned Socialist Party treasurer and MP Laszlo Boldvai, suspected of abuse of influence in the Tocsik affair.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Industrial production in January was up 11 percent compared to the previous month and by 6.4 percent on a year earlier, the Central Statistics Office reports.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The German firm Klockner Stahl und Metallhandel has probably won the tender aimed at selling 78.5 percent of the metal trading company Ferroglobus Rt.
- Zalakeramia Rt. has bought 51 percent of the industrial ceramics manufacturer Pietra Rt., the only firm of its kind in Eastern Europe, said Zalakeramia vice president Sandor Jellen.
- The pre-tax profit of Daewoo Bank Rt. increased by 29 percent to HUF 1.36 billion last year.
- The total 1996 revenue of the First American Hungarian Insurance Co. came to HUF 2.75 billion, said president R. K. Nottingham.

- The Metropolitan Court declared Friday that the State Privatisation & Holding Co. has until April 15 to make a statement on what resources were used to pay HUF 804 million to lawyer Marta Tocsik for negotiating municipal land deals.
